column1: # Ground truth for formatColor(), generated from meo-canvas v1's built module
# (`dist/esm/animate/color.js`) rather than from either v2 implementation.
# v1 at tag v9.0.2, commit 890eed2, working tree clean -- the same provenance
# the four original tables name, and verified rather than assumed: this
# generator was first run against those tables and reproduced all 612 of their
# rows exactly, which is what establishes it is the same v1 they came from.
# Neither surface may be written from the other: a misreading of v1 that reaches
# both looks like agreement. Both are written against this, and this came from
# v1 running, not from anyone reading it.
# Values are shortest-round-trip decimals, compared exactly. There is no
# tolerance here.
# **JavaScript-only.** There is no string emitter anywhere in
# `meo-canvas-core`: its nearest thing is `Rgba::to_color`, which returns
# four clamped bytes. So this table has a JavaScript walker and no Rust one,
# and the absence is itself the finding rather than an oversight.
# The out-of-gamut rows are the point: hex cannot hold a channel above 255
# or below 0, and clamping would substitute a duller colour without saying
# so. Rust preserves the same overshoot right up to the byte boundary and
# only JavaScript can express what is past it.
